correctness.rationale: For every positive-infection edge the contact equilibrium denominator is strictly positive on K because creation is positive for nonsaturated prevalence; this gives a continuous T:K->K. Continuity at zero yields T(y)=D^{-1}My+o(||y||), and a positive PF left eigenvector gives weighted expansion whenever R0>1. Brouwer fixed points of (1-eps)T+eps a cannot approach zero; a nonzero limiting fixed point exists and is strictly positive by directed strong connectivity. Exact rational example and 7959 independent exact assertions support, but do not prove, the general analytic claim.

originality.rationale: The identical model source explicitly conjectures the desired spectral-radius endemic existence criterion and proves only a stronger row/column-sum sufficient condition. This theorem establishes the implication with an explicit positive-interior contact renewal assumption and without monotonicity, using a Perron-weighted topological argument. Different state-feedback SIS works and semantic mathematical records have no covering statement identified. A generic positive-map implication or unindexed later proof is residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed general cone-map fixed-point theorems might imply the abstract implication; the new contribution is its proof for the specified adaptive epidemic model and natural positivity class.
Unrestricted contact creation that vanishes in the interior is not covered; the source conjecture in complete generality remains unproved here.

value.rationale: The source expressly identifies R0>1 endemic existence as an unresolved spectral threshold. The proof substitutes global Perron expansion plus Brouwer fixed points for the paper’s stronger coordinatewise row/column condition; this is necessary in heterogeneous networks with individually subcritical rows, as the exact sqrt(12) versus 2/7 witness shows. The result covers all strongly connected finite directed networks with continuous positive contact renewal, and does not claim global stability.
